rubricDispositions.rationale: Stable source, observation, revision, unit, and job keys are derived from structured tenant/connection-generation/channel/provider fields without Convex IDs; binding checks reject cross-tenant and cross-channel captures before rows are staged.

The schema/helper slice requires a verified Slack channel binding matching organization, connection, generation, team, app, bot, channel, and external channel before accepting capture input; no caller-facing authorization bypass is added.

New content-bearing rows carry explicit lifecycle envelopes, start active, document tombstone/redaction/purge progression and rollback retention, and the focused transaction proof shows partial failures leave no orphan ledger rows.

Content-bearing revisions are schema-versioned and lifecycle-fenced for later redaction and purge, while receipt audit rows remain separate from normalized text/blocks; the reviewed slice adds no raw provider payload logging or secret exposure.

Duplicate replay validation fences the observed revision but not the derived source unit or assembly job intent; changed effectKey or threadKey can alter assembly intent while still returning duplicate.
Transport replay does not converge on exactly one assembly intent because duplicate validation omits assemblyJobKey/sourceUnitKey from the replay binding.
The production migration runtime is not fenced to the task-owned extracted executable modules, and duplicate source-ledger replay is not fenced to one assembly source unit/job intent.

S05-T01 adds schema definitions, Confect table definitions, migration fragments/runtime extraction, generator code, and focused tests only; it does not introduce a live provider SDK import, secret read, webhook handler, outbound adapter, or provider payload logging surface.

findings.summary: Executable migration extraction is not wired into production runtime imports
findings.details: S05-T01 requires S00/S01 executable migration bodies to be extracted into task-owned modules and wired through production. However migrations.impl.ts still imports probeExpand, probeFail, stableTenantOrganizationKeysExpand, and stableTenantWorkspaceKeysExpand from ./migrations, so the extracted migration-implementations/S00-T04.ts and S01-T02.ts bodies are never used by the production registry. This defeats the migration ownership boundary and leaves future production execution coupled to the legacy monolithic module.

findings.summary: Duplicate transport replay is not fenced to one assembly intent
findings.details: Duplicate delivery validation records only deliveryKey plus observationKey and sourceRevisionKey. sourceLedgerKeysFor derives sourceUnitKey from threadKey and assemblyJobKey from effectKey, but assertValidSourceLedgerCapture does not bind either value into duplicate replay validation. The same transport delivery can replay with the same observation/revision but changed effectKey or threadKey, return outcome duplicate, and produce a different assembly job/source unit intent, violating the task requirement that duplicate receipts converge on one logical observation/source revision and assembly intent.
